On 27 June, 2024 when the present proceedings were taken up and as the petitioners were yet to be paid land acquisition compensation, we had passed the following order:
 1.
Mr. Venegavkar, learned counsel for the Respondents fairly states  that compensation would be paid to the Petitioners in the manner  known to law along with whatever accrued interest.

If that be so, learned  counsel for Petitioners states that the Petitioners are ready and willing to  hand over the physical possession of the property on receipt of the  compensation and also comply with the obligations under the Award, in  accordance with law.

2. Stand over to 11 July 2024, High On Board.
3.
Thereafter the proceedings were listed before us on 12 July, 2024.

Insofar as the alternate residential premises/tenement to be allotted to the petitioners and the premises being ready and to be handed over to the petitioners by the respondent/authority as also considering the difference in the calculation of the compensation amount, we had passed the following order so that the issues can be settled:
 1.

In our order dated 27 June, 2024 we had recorded the statement as  made by Mr. Venegaonkar, learned counsel for the respondents that the  compensation will be paid to the petitioners in the manner known to law  along with whatever accrued interest.

We had accordingly adjourned the  proceedings observing that considering the position taken by the  respondents, the petitioners were ready and willing to handover the  possession of the property on receipt of the compensation and also  comply with the obligations under the award in accordance with law.
2. Today we are informed by Mr. Venegaonkar that the amount to be  disbursed to the petitioners is already calculated.
There appears to be  some issue on the interest amount.

We have already observed in our Savita Rasiklal Mandan And Anr vs Union Of India And Anr on 8 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46673144/
2  order that accrued interest whatever payable to the petitioners will be in  accordance with law.

As seen from the aforesaid order, the dispute which was sought to be raised by the petitioners was in regard to the plinth area.

Learned counsel for the respondent/UOI has placed before us an affidavit as also the photographs of the tenement which is ready to be occupied and which appears to be absolutely brand new newly constructed premises.
The petitioners have taken inspection and have disputed the plinth area.
On such backdrop, we heard the proceedings on 25 July, 2024.
As the only issue which remained was in regard to the measurement of the plinth of the tenement, we thought it can also be put to rest.

We had accordingly passed the following order:
1. In pursuance of our order dated 18 July 2024, learned counsel for the petitioners has placed on record affidavit of petitioner no.1.
Copy of the same is also furnished to advocate for the respondent-Union of India.
Let the advocate for the respondent-Union of India take appropriate instructions.
2. An affidavit on behalf of the respondent-Union of India is also placed on record and copy of the same is being served on the advocate for the petitioners.

3. Accordingly, stand over to 01 August 2024 (H.O.B.).

7.
The position on record, as clearly seen from the affidavit of the respondents is that the plinth area is in accordance with the award, having no discrepancy.
The petitioners, however, are not satisfied on the plinth area, even after an affidavit is placed on record by the UT Administration, along with appropriate certification of the plinth area.
The petitioners on the basis of advice received by them intend to dispute the plinth area and as to what has been urged on behalf of UT Administration in that regard.

On such backdrop, the proceedings were listed before us on 1 August, 2024 when we passed the following order:
8 August, 2024 4.WP3969_2021.DOC "1.
As a matter of last chance, to enable the Advocate for the petitioners to consider the respondents' affidavit, stand over to 8 August, 2024 (First on Board).
No further adjournments.

2. Ad-interim order, if any granted earlier, shall continue to operate till the adjourned date of hearing."
8.
It is on the aforesaid premise, the proceedings are before us.
Today again Mr. Shah is before the Court to contend that the petitioners are not satisfied with the measurement of plinth area.

He has also contended and surprisingly for the first time, a grievance is made that a letter of allotment of alternate premises is not issued to the petitioner, this despite the petitioners being aware of the allotment as also being given access to the premises as earmarked for their allotment.
Considering this, we passed over the proceedings to be taken up in the post session, calling upon the learned counsel for the UT Administration to place on record the allotment order.
Accordingly, allotment letter dated 5 August, 2024 issued by the Collector, Diu is placed on record as also a copy of the same is handed over to Mr. Shah, learned counsel for the petitioners.

9. In the facts and circumstances of the case, we are of the clear opinion that it would be difficult for us to examine the contentions of the petitioners on the dispute in regard to the area of the plinth.

This would be clearly a disputed question of fact, which is called upon to be gone into the proceeding of a Writ Petition, despite the certification of the plinth area on affidavit by the respondents.

Insofar as the prayers are concerned, we have observed that the monetary compensation has already been received by the petitioners, as also a newly constructed tenement, is being sought to be handed to the petitioner.
In these circumstances, further adjudication of the petition is not called for.
We would certainly not examine any disputed question of fact in the present proceeding.
